                   21   1.     PURPOSE
                   22          This Order will govern discovery of electronically stored information (“ESI”) in this case
                   23   as a supplement to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, this Court’s Guidelines for the Discovery
                   24   of Electronically Stored Information, and any other applicable orders and rules.
                   25   2.     COOPERATION
                   26          The parties are aware of the importance the Court places on cooperation and commit to
                   27   cooperate in good faith throughout the matter consistent with this Court’s Guidelines for the
                   28   Discovery of ESI.

                    1   3.     LIAISON
                    2          The parties have identified liaisons to each other who are and will be knowledgeable
                    3   about and responsible for discussing their respective ESI. Each e-discovery liaison will be, or
                    4   have access to those who are, knowledgeable about the technical aspects of e-discovery,
                    5   including the location, nature, accessibility, format, collection, search methodologies, and
                    6   production of ESI in this matter. The parties will rely on the liaisons, as needed, to confer about
                    7   ESI and to help resolve disputes without court intervention.
                    8   4.     PRESERVATION
                    9          The parties have discussed their preservation obligations and needs and agree that
                   10   preservation of potentially relevant ESI will be reasonable and proportionate. To reduce the
                   11   costs and burdens of preservation and to ensure proper ESI is preserved, the parties agree that:
                   12          (a)     The parties will exchange a list of the types of ESI they believe should be preserved
                   13   and the custodians, or general job titles or descriptions of custodians, for whom they believe ESI
                   14   should be preserved, e.g., “HR head,” “scientist,” and “marketing manager.” The parties shall add
                   15   or remove custodians as reasonably necessary;
                   16          (b)     The parties will identify the number of legal hold recipients for whom ESI is being
                   17   preserved.
                   18          (c)     The parties are currently meeting and conferring regarding the temporal scope of
                   19   ESI preservation and, following the parties’ agreement and/or a Court order, the parties will file an
                   20   amended stipulation.
                   21          (d)     The parties will continue to meet and confer, where appropriate, regarding ESI
                   22   preservation, the temporal scope of ESI preservation and/or production, and in connection with
                   23   other matters, consistent with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, this Court’s Civil Local Rules,
                   24   and any other applicable orders and rules.
                   25   5.     SEARCH
                   26          The parties agree that in responding to Fed. R. Civ. P. 34 requests, or earlier if
                   27   appropriate, they will meet and confer about methods to search ESI in order to identify ESI that
                   28   is subject to production in discovery and filter out ESI that is not subject to discovery.

                    1   6.     PRODUCTION FORMATS
                    2          The parties agree to produce documents in TIFF and/or native file formats in accordance
                    3   with the requirements below. If particular documents warrant a different format, the parties will
                    4   cooperate to arrange for the mutually acceptable production of such documents. The parties
                    5   agree not to degrade the searchability of documents as part of the document production process.
                    6          (a)     De-duplication. The parties will use industry standard MD5 or SHA hash values at
                    7   the Family level to globally deduplicate all files identified for production. Stand-alone ESI will not
                    8   be compared to email attachments for deduplication purposes. Hard copy documents containing
                    9   handwritten notes will not be considered as duplicative of any other document.
                   10          (b)     Document Unitization. Where documents with attachments are produced, they
                   11   will be attached in the same manner as included in the original file. Unless withheld documents
                   12   contain solely privileged information, or other information protected from disclosure, any party
                   13   producing documents (“Producing Party”) will produce complete document families where any
                   14   portion of the family contains relevant information. Where documents are produced and the full
                   15   family is not included, the Producing Party will identify the missing attachments by means of a
                   16   “place holder” file explaining why the document was not produced.
                   17          Where the Producing Party converts hard copy documents into electronic format,
                   18   distinct documents must not be merged into a single record, and single documents must not be
                   19   split into multiple records.
                   20          Hard copy documents that are segregated or separated from other documents, whether
                   21   by inclusion of binders, files, dividers, tabs, clips or any other method, will be produced in a
                   22   manner that reflects these divisions.
                   23          (c)     Production Delivery. Productions shall be delivered via secure online data transfer
                   24   or on an external hard drive if the size of a production makes online transfer impractical.
                   25          (d)     Encryption. To maximize the security of information in transit, the parties shall
                   26   encrypt any physical media used for production. The Producing Party will provide the encryption
                   27   key or password and instructions to the party receiving the documents (“Receiving Party”), upon
                   28   receipt of the encrypted media.

                    2              i.        TIFF images will be produced in black and white, 300x300 dpi Group IV

                    4              ii.       Images will include the following content where present:
                    5                               a.    For word processing files (e.g., Microsoft Word):

                    6                        content.
                    7                              b.       For presentation files (e.g., Microsoft PowerPoint):
                    8                        Speaker notes, comments, and all other hidden content.

                    9                                c.      For spreadsheet files (e.g., Microsoft Excel – if
                                             applicable): Hidden columns, rows, and sheets; comments, and any
                   10                        similar in-line editing or hidden content.
                   11              iii.      The parties may request color copies of any documents that cannot be

                   12              accurately reviewed in black and white TIFF format. Reasonable requests for

                   13              color documents should not be refused.

                   14              iv.       The parties will meet and confer to discuss a suitable production format

                   15              for any proprietary or non-standard file types that require special software or

                   16              technical knowledge for review, databases and database reports, and any

                   17              document types that cannot be accurately rendered or reviewed in TIFF image

                   18              format.

                   19              (f)       Native Production Requirements.

                   20              i.        Spreadsheets files (e.g., Microsoft Excel and .csv files) shall be provided

                   21                        in Native Format with a single placeholder image bearing the Bates

                   22                        number and confidentiality designation.

                   23               ii.      When redaction of a spreadsheet is necessary in image format, a redacted

                   24                        full TIFF version may be produced if the spreadsheet is manually

                   25                        formatted for optimal printing. If the spreadsheet requiring redaction is

                   26                        not reasonably usable in TIFF format, the parties will meet and confer to

                   27                        determine a suitable production format.

                    2                            redact privileged information from documents produced in native format

                    4                      iv.   Media files (e.g. .mp3, .wmv, etc.) will be produced in native format with
                    5                            a single placeholder image bearing the Bates number and confidentiality

                    7                  (g)       Load Files. A Concordance compatible data load file will be provided with
                    8   each production volume containing a header row listing all metadata fields included in the volume.
                    9   Image load files will be produced in Concordance/Opticon compatible format.
                   10                  (h)       Extracted Text/OCR
                   11                  i.        The parties will not degrade the searchability of documents as part of the
                   12                            document production process. Electronically extracted text shall be provided
                   13                            if available for documents collected from electronic sources. Text generated
                   14                            via optical character recognition (“OCR”) shall be provided for all ESI that
                   15                            does not contain electronically extractable text (e.g., non-searchable PDF
                   16                            files or JPG images), documents redacted in image format, and hard copy
                   17                            documents.
                   18                  ii.       Document text will be produced as separate, document-level text files and
                   19                            will not be embedded in the metadata load file.
                   20                  iii.      Text files will be named according to the beginning Bates number of the
                   21                  document to which they correspond.
                   22                  (i)       Metadata.      The parties agree to produce the metadata fields listed in
                   23   Appendix A where available. Parties are not obligated to produce metadata that is not reasonably
                   24   available. Parties are not required to convert files, documents, or data to create or add metadata that
                   25   is not part of the way such information is stored in the ordinary course of business.
                   26                  (j)       Confidentiality Designations. If a party converts native files or other
                   27   ESI that bear a confidentiality designation under the Protective Order entered in this case to
                   28   hardcopy form, such party shall mark the physical document with the same confidentiality

                    2   all produced files or documents shall be marked with the appropriate confidentiality designation

                    4   7.      DOCUMENTS PROTECTED FROM DISCOVERY
                    5                  (a)     Pursuant to Fed. R. Evid. 502(d), the production of a privileged or work-
                    6   product-protected document, whether inadvertent or otherwise, is not a waiver of privilege or
                    7   protection from discovery in this case or in any other federal or state proceeding. This Order shall
                    8   be interpreted to provide the maximum protection allowed by Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d).
                    9   The provisions of Federal Rule of Evidence 502(b) do not apply.
                   10                  (b)     This Order will not serve to limit a party’s right to conduct a review of
                   11   documents, ESI or information (including metadata) for relevance, responsiveness and/or
                   12   segregation of privileged information before production. The parties further agree that, upon being
                   13   notified of a Producing Party’s disclosure of privileged and/or protected documents, ESI or
                   14   information (including metadata), the Receiving Party must take the steps set forth in Federal Rule
                   15   of Civil Procedure 26(b)(5)(B), including, but not limited to, promptly returning, sequestering, or
                   16   destroying the specified documents, ESI or information (including metadata) and any copies it may
                   17   have.
                   18                  (c)     Communications involving trial counsel that post-date the filing of the
                   19   complaint need not be placed on a privilege log. Communications may be identified on a privilege
                   20   log by category, rather than individually, if appropriate.
                   21   8.      MODIFICATION
                   22           This Order may be modified by a stipulated order of the parties or by the Court for good

                   23   cause shown.

                   24   9.      MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

                   25                  (a)     No Waiver. Nothing in this Order shall be interpreted to require disclosure

                   26   of information that is not relevant or proportional to the needs of the case, or information protected

                   27   by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or

                   28   immunity. The parties do not waive objections as to the production, discoverability, admissibility

                                  17                                                THE JURY

                                  18          The Jury Office asks prospective jurors to complete an online jury questionnaire in

                                  19   advance of their summons date. The standard questionnaire available on the Northern District’s

                                  20   website at http://www.cand.uscourts.gov/wp-content/uploads/attorneys/Internet-version_Standard-

                                  21   CAND-Trial_SurveyMonkey_3-2022.pdf. The parties are allowed to add 10 case specific

                                  22   questions to the questionnaire. The parties shall meet and confer, and to the extent possible, file a

                                  23   joint list of proposed questions to add to the questionnaire. To the extent that the parties cannot

                                  24   agree, they may submit separate proposed questions from which the Court will choose 10. The

                                  25   parties joint or separate submissions are due 21 days before trial. The Court will provide the

                                  26   parties with the survey responses the Friday before trial.

                                  27          In civil cases, there are no alternate jurors and the jury is selected as follows: Eighteen to

                                  28   twenty jurors are called to fill the jury box and the row in front of the bar, and are given numbers

                                   1   (1 through 20). The remaining potential jurors will be seated in the public benches. Hardship

                                   2   excuses will usually be considered at this point. Counsel may conduct a limited voir dire.

                                   4   will consider whether to fill in the seats of the stricken jurors. If so, questions will be asked of the

                                   5   additional jurors and cause motions as to them will be considered. After a short recess, each side

                                   6   may exercise its allotment of peremptory challenges out of the presence of the potential jurors.

                                   7   The eight (or such other size as will constitute the jury) surviving the challenge process with the

                                   8   lowest numbers become the final jury. If more (or fewer) than eight jurors are to be seated, then

                                   9   the starting number will be adjusted. So too if more than a total of six peremptories are allowed.

                                  11   in the jury box and sworn. The Court may alter this procedure in its discretion and after

                                  12   consultation with the parties.
